note.en: Ekalavya trains before a clay image of Drona and, when asked, gives his right thumb as guru-dakshina, though Drona had refused to formally accept him

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Section CXXXIV ("If thou art really my pupil, give me then my fees"..."Ekalavya...cut off without ado his thumb, and gave it unto Drona")

verification.notes: Relation read against ganguli-mahabharata Adi Parva, Section CXXXIV ("If thou art really my pupil, give me then my fees"..."Ekalavya...cut off without ado his thumb, and gave it unto Drona"); endpoints and type confirmed in the primary text.

note.en: Drona demands Ekalavya's thumb as guru-dakshina to remove the threat he posed to Arjuna's claim of being the finest archer

verification.notes: Relation read against ganguli-mahabharata Adi Parva, Section CXXXIV; endpoints and type confirmed in the primary text.
